weather.tip: Rain chance is at 96% today — carry an umbrella, wear shoes you don't mind getting wet, and budget extra time for the commute since waterlogging-prone stretches slow down fast once showers start.

around.headline: 39 arrested, drugs worth ₹55.80 crore seized in citywide crackdown
around.summary: Bengaluru police carried out a major operation seizing narcotics worth ₹55.80 crore and arresting 39 people across the city. It's a reminder that drug rackets often operate out of ordinary-looking rented flats and PGs — report suspicious activity to your local police station.

around.headline: Bengaluru man kills two daughters, attempts suicide at 5-star hotel
around.summary: A man staying at a hotel near the airport killed his two young daughters and attempted suicide; police say a note found at the scene pointed to a marital dispute. If you or someone you know is in emotional distress, Tele-MANAS (14416) offers free, confidential mental health support 24/7.

around.headline: CAG flags ₹6,603 crore land-cost overrun in Bengaluru Metro Phases 1 and 2
around.summary: A CAG audit found planning lapses inflated land acquisition costs for Metro Phases 1 and 2 by about ₹6,600 crore, and flagged poor Metro-BMTC integration for missed ridership targets; separately, the planned Orange Line double-decker stretch may shrink from 37km to 11km. Don't expect the newer lines to ease congestion as fast as promised.

around.headline: Bengaluru ranked India's most congested city
around.summary: A new TomTom traffic index places Bengaluru at the top of India's congestion rankings. Nothing commuters don't already feel, but it's a good prompt to build extra buffer time into today's travel, especially with heavy rain forecast.

around.headline: Vacant site owners face cleanup bills crossing ₹1 lakh
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has warned owners of vacant sites (like standard 40x60 plots) that garbage cleanup charges have crossed ₹1 lakh, running up to ₹1.7 lakh for larger or repeat-offending plots. If you own an empty site, get it fenced and cleared before the next inspection round.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Parliament clears taxation bill; UPI to remain free
around.summary: The Finance Minister confirmed in Parliament that UPI transactions will continue to be free for users, though no final framework on merchant discount rate (MDR) has been settled yet. Your day-to-day UPI payments aren't getting a fee anytime soon.

around.headline: US court ends all criminal charges against Gautam Adani
around.summary: A US court has dropped all criminal charges against Gautam Adani, his brother Sagar Adani, and associate Vneet Jaain. The move removes a major legal overhang for the Adani group, which could ease pressure on its stock and bond prices in the coming days.

street_smart.title: You're at a park or a fun-run when a fellow runner ahead of you suddenly collapses, unresponsive, and doesn't seem to be breathing normally. A small crowd gathers but no one moves. What do you do first?
street_smart.based_on: A participant died of cardiac arrest during the Nandi Hills monsoon marathon this weekend (The Hindu, Aug 9) — medical emergency response hasn't come up in recent briefs, so it rotates in from the evergreen list.
street_smart.situation: The runner is on the ground, not responding when you call out or tap their shoulder, and their breathing looks abnormal or absent. Someone nearby suggests propping him up and giving him water; another says to wait for a doctor since none of you are trained.

choices.text: Prop him up against a tree and get someone to pour water on his face or into his mouth to revive him.
choices.feedback: This doesn't address cardiac arrest at all and can actively hurt him — pouring water into the mouth of an unresponsive person risks choking, and propping him up does nothing to restore blood flow to the brain and heart. Every second spent on this delays the one thing that actually helps.

choices.text: Check for a response and normal breathing, call 108 immediately and put it on speaker, then start hard, fast chest compressions if he isn't breathing normally — continue until help or an AED arrives.
choices.feedback: Correct. Sudden cardiac arrest needs immediate hands-only CPR; survival odds drop by roughly 10% for every minute without compressions, so acting in the first minute matters more than technique being perfect. Calling 108 on speaker lets the dispatcher talk you through it in real time.

choices.text: Hold off on touching him and wait for a doctor or someone with formal CPR training to arrive, since you don't want to make things worse.
choices.feedback: Hands-only CPR from an untrained bystander is far better than no CPR at all, and waiting for a 'qualified' person burns exactly the minutes that determine survival. Dispatchers on 108 will walk anyone through the compressions in real time.

choices.text: Start filming the scene on your phone so there's a record for the medical team when they arrive, then go look for an ambulance nearby.
choices.feedback: Filming wastes precious time and going off to search for an ambulance means no one is doing compressions in the meantime; call 108 to bring help to you instead of leaving to find it, and start compressions immediately.

takeaways: For any collapse with no response and no normal breathing, call 108 immediately and put the phone on speaker so you can start hands-only CPR while getting real-time guidance.
Push hard and fast in the center of the chest at 100-120 compressions per minute — untrained bystander CPR is far better than waiting for someone 'qualified'.
Look for a public AED (automated external defibrillator) at malls, metro stations, or event first-aid tents — using one alongside CPR significantly improves survival odds.

quiz.question: A CAG audit found planning lapses inflated the land acquisition cost for Bengaluru Metro Phases 1 and 2 by roughly how much?
quiz.why: The same CAG report also flagged that Metro ridership has consistently missed its original 2007 projections, even as of 2023, partly due to poor integration with BMTC bus routes.

quiz.question: A new TomTom traffic index ranked Bengaluru as India's _____ city.
quiz.why: Bengaluru has repeatedly topped or near-topped national and global congestion indices in recent years as vehicle registrations have outpaced road and transit capacity growth.

quiz.question: A US court recently dropped all criminal charges against which Indian businessman and his associates?
quiz.why: The charges, filed in a New York court, had alleged bribery and securities fraud tied to a solar energy contracts case; their dismissal removes a major legal overhang for the Adani group.

quiz.question: Which free, 24/7 national helpline connects callers to India's Tele-MANAS mental health support service?
quiz.why: 108 is India's medical/police/fire emergency number, while 1930 is the separate national cybercrime helpline for reporting financial fraud.

quiz.question: During hands-only CPR on an adult, chest compressions should be given at roughly what rate per minute?
quiz.why: This is close to the tempo of the song 'Stayin' Alive' by the Bee Gees, which CPR trainers often use to help people keep the right pace.
